"'''Keep On Loving You'''" is a [[rock ballad|ballad]] written by [[Kevin Cronin]] and performed by American rock band [[REO Speedwagon]]. It features the lead guitar work of [[Gary Richrath]]. The song first appeared on REO Speedwagon's 1980 album ''[[Hi Infidelity]]''. 

It was the first REO Speedwagon single to break the top 50 on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], reaching the number-one spot for one week in March 1981.<ref>[[List of Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles of 1981]]</ref> The single was certified platinum for U.S. sales of over one million copies. It peaked at number seven on the [[UK Singles Chart]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.officialcharts.com/artist/18939%2Freo-speedwagon/ |title=Reo Speedwagon | Artist |publisher=Official Charts |access-date=December 9, 2017}}</ref> 

"Keep On Loving You" has been a mainstay on 1980s [[soft rock]] [[compilation album|compilations]] and has appeared on dozens of 'various artists' compilation albums, as well as several REO Speedwagon greatest hits albums.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.allmusic.com/song/keep-on-loving-you-mt0000472471| title = REO Speedwagon, Keep On Loving You (Appears On)| access-date = February 12, 2015 | work = [[AllMusic]] | publisher = [[Rovi Corporation]]}}</ref> ''[[Ultimate Classic Rock]]'' critic Matt Wardlaw rated it REO Speedwagon's all-time greatest song.<ref name=ucr>{{cite web|title=Top 10 REO Speedwagon Songs|author=Wardlaw, Matt|date=October 6, 2013|accessdate=February 22, 2023|url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/reo-speedwagon-songs/|publisher=[[Ultimate Classic Rock]]}}</ref>

"Keep On Loving You" is a ballad written by Kevin Cronin and performed by American rock band REO Speedwagon. It features the lead guitar work of Gary Richrath. The song first appeared on REO Speedwagon's 1980 album Hi Infidelity. 

It was the first REO Speedwagon single to break the top 50 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100, reaching the number-one spot for one week in March 1981. The single was certified platinum for U.S. sales of over one million copies. It peaked at number seven on the UK Singles Chart. 

"Keep On Loving You" has been a mainstay on 1980s soft rock compilations and has appeared on dozens of 'various artists' compilation albums, as well as several REO Speedwagon greatest hits albums. Ultimate Classic Rock critic Matt Wardlaw rated it REO Speedwagon's all-time greatest song.

sections.heading: Background and recording
sections.wikitext:
Kevin Cronin was inspired to write "Keep On Loving You" after learning that his wife had cheated on him.<ref name=ucr2>{{cite web|title=50 Greatest Power Ballads in Rock History Ranked|author=Irwin, Corey|date=June 3, 2025|access-date=2025-12-03|publisher=[[Ultimate Classic Rock]]|url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/greatest-power-ballads/}}</ref>. He said that the song affirmed his belief that people can change, and if a relationship is worth saving then you should "give it all you've got."<ref name=ucr2/>

Cronin stated that he wrote "Keep On Loving You" as a more traditional love ballad, and the band as a whole developed it into its final arrangement as a [[power ballad]]. He recounted: {{quote|I walked into rehearsal and sat down at the piano, which I rarely do because I'm a guitar player, and started playing "Keep on Loving You." ... And the guys in the band looked at me like I was from another planet. They were like, "What are you...?" because we were all bringing in songs for this record we were going to make and they looked at me like I was crazy. And I'm like, "Dude, this song really means a lot to me." [And they said] "So, dude, that's not an REO Speedwagon song." And I kind of was like, "You know what? I'm the main songwriter for REO Speedwagon, so if I write a song, it's an REO Speedwagon song. It's the band's job to turn it into an REO Speedwagon song." I was so passionate about this song. Everyone kind of got it and sure enough, Gary [Richrath] went over, plugged in his guitar and started playing power chords to this little love song I wrote. The next thing we knew, it was a number one record and everyone was calling it a power ballad and acted like we had this strategy for success that made this song happen when really it was just an accident.<ref>{{cite web |first=Zach |last=Everson |url=https://archive.louisville.com/content/reo-speedwagons-kevin-cronin-louisville-power-ballads-and-if-my-wifes-slut |title=REO Speedwagon's Kevin Cronin on Louisville, power ballads and if my wife's a slut |work=[[Louisville (magazine)|Louisville]] |date=February 24, 2010 |access-date=February 24, 2010 |archive-date=June 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120623120047/http://www.louisville.com/content/reo-speedwagons-kevin-cronin-louisville-power-ballads-and-if-my-wifes-slut |url-status=live }}</ref>}}

Cronin said that he started playing the chords for the song on piano, which he had done "about 100 times" before without anyone else noticing, but one time [[Gary Richrath]] started playing on his [[Gibson Les Paul|Les Paul]] guitar. Cronin initially thought that Richrath was playing just to drown him out, but he then realized that "That's exactly what this song needs!", after which Cronin said that "the song took off from there."<ref name=classic>{{cite web|title=The 10 Best REO Speedwagon Songs, by Kevin Cronin|date=May 11, 2016|work=[[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]]|access-date=2022-06-19|last=Cronin|first=Kevin|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/reospeedwagon-bestofeverything}}</ref> He claimed that before that the band felt the song sounded too much like [[Barry Manilow]] and that after the addition of Richrath's guitar chords he recognized that the original version sounded too sweet.<ref>{{cite web|title=REO Speedwagon: We Thought Every Album Would Sell 10 Million Copies...|author=Elliott, Paul|publisher=Louder Sound|work=[[Classic Rock (magazine)|Classic Rock]]|access-date=June 17, 2026|date=November 20, 2015|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/reo-speedwagon-we-thought-every-album-would-sell-10-million-copies}}</ref>

[[Epic Records]] did not think the song was good enough to be released as a single, but the band persuaded them to do so.<ref name=classic />

Cronin stated that he wrote "Keep On Loving You" as a more traditional love ballad, and the band as a whole developed it into its final arrangement as a power ballad. He recounted: {{quote|I walked into rehearsal and sat down at the piano, which I rarely do because I'm a guitar player, and started playing "Keep on Loving You." ... And the guys in the band looked at me like I was from another planet. They were like, "What are you...?" because we were all bringing in songs for this record we were going to make and they looked at me like I was crazy. And I'm like, "Dude, this song really means a lot to me." [And they said] "So, dude, that's not an REO Speedwagon song." And I kind of was like, "You know what? I'm the main songwriter for REO Speedwagon, so if I write a song, it's an REO Speedwagon song. It's the band's job to turn it into an REO Speedwagon song." I was so passionate about this song. Everyone kind of got it and sure enough, Gary [Richrath] went over, plugged in his guitar and started playing power chords to this little love song I wrote. The next thing we knew, it was a number one record and everyone was calling it a power ballad and acted like we had this strategy for success that made this song happen when really it was just an accident.}}

Cronin said that he started playing the chords for the song on piano, which he had done "about 100 times" before without anyone else noticing, but one time Gary Richrath started playing on his Les Paul guitar. Cronin initially thought that Richrath was playing just to drown him out, but he then realized that "That's exactly what this song needs!", after which Cronin said that "the song took off from there." He claimed that before that the band felt the song sounded too much like Barry Manilow and that after the addition of Richrath's guitar chords he recognized that the original version sounded too sweet.

Epic Records did not think the song was good enough to be released as a single, but the band persuaded them to do so.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
"Keep On Loving You" received mixed to negative reviews from critics and audiences alike; it has been widely criticized for its dated and bombastic production style, sentimental lyrics, perceived "overplayed" nature and lack of originality.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/hi-infidelity-mw0000191545 |title=Hi-Infidelity - REO Speedwagon |date=June 6, 2012 |website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref>

Stephen Thomas Erlewine of AllMusic gave the song a positive review and said, "And so what if it does, because this is great arena rock, filled with hooks as expansive as Three Rivers Stadium and as catchy as the flu. That, of course, applies to the record's two biggest hits—the power ballad "Keep on Loving You" and the surging "Take It on the Run"—which define their era, but what gives the album real staying power is that the rest of the record works equally well."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/hi-infidelity-mw0000191545 |title=Hi-Infidelity - REO Speedwagon |date=June 6, 2012 |website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref> 

Mike DeGagne criticized the song for giving the band "more appeal to FM radio and more commercial success", but also praised its instrumentation, describing it as "keyboard-guided melodies of its type, set adrift to Kevin Cronin's gentle, comfy-cozy vocals" and assuring that "No matter which instrument's riffs are heard, guitar or keyboard, they're polished and pristine, blanketed by lyrics that are simple yet overwhelmingly emotive."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/song/keep-on-loving-you-mt0000472471 |title=Keep on Loving You - REO Speedwagon |date=April 3, 2013|website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=November 9, 2025}}</ref>

In 2025 ''Ultimate Classic Rock'' critic Corey Irwin rated "Keep on Loving You" as the 11th greatest power ballad of all time.<ref name=ucr2/> In 2013 ''Ultimate Classic Rock'' critic Matt Wardlaw rated it as REO Speedwagon's greatest song.<ref name=ucr/>

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: In 1981, a video of the song was the 17th played on the [[First music videos aired on MTV|first day of broadcast]] of [[MTV]], on August 1.<ref>{{cite web| url= http://jmedinalive.com/2011/06/random-facts-1st-video-to-ever-play-on-mtv/ | title= Random Facts: 1st Video to Ever Play on MTV| website= JMedinaLive.com | date= June 8, 2011 | access-date= January 14, 2015}}</ref> It was framed by a scene of Kevin Cronin talking about his relationship troubles with a female psychiatrist and contained a shot where a woman picked up a telephone connected to Gary Richrath's guitar, referencing the live version of "[[157 Riverside Avenue]]”.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wJzNZ1c5C9c |title=REO Speedwagon, Keep On Loving You|publisher=[[YouTube]] |date=October 9, 2013 |access-date=February 13, 2015}}</ref>
